newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-U.S. data spark share slump but aids dollar.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-U.S. data spark share slump but aids dollar.

text.p: European stock and bond markets went into reatreat but the dollar rallied on Thursday after U.S. economic data appeared to strengthen the case for a rise in American interest rates.
Wall Street was more than 50 points down as European markets closed with the German bourse leading the declines.

The dollar jumped back over 1.70 marks and 123 yen after the foreign exchange market saw strong U.S. retail sales data and a bigger than expected fall in weekly jobless claims as pointing to a rate rise. But U.S. treasury bonds fell, dragging stocks down with them.

"Bonds are pulling stocks down. The market is high, and the economic news this morning raises fresh fears of an interest rate hike, Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments in New York, said.

Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich said the 0.8 percent rise in retail sales figures for February showed the U.S. economy in the first quarter looked "very strong" with consumers going "gangbusters" on spending.

"These data greatly increase the likelihood of first quarter GDP of four percent and as such, must be seen as increasing the likelihood of a Fed tightening," said Jeremy Hawkins, senior economic advisor at Bank of America in London.
The Federal Reserve's Open Market Committee (FOMC) is due to meet on March 25.
Coming on top of Wall Street's losing performance on Wednesday, the Dow's renewed weakness topped a poor day for Europe's major bourses.
The London and Paris markets fell, but their declines were nowhere as bad as Frankfurt where floor trade ended with the 30-share DAX index losing 1.92 percent to 3,349.81.

Frankfurt's losses were extended in later screen trading, with the IBIS DAX ending down 14.58 points at 3,367.82, and analysts predicted the German bourse was likely to remain under pressure in the near-term.
Some traders argued, however, that the losses were not particularly dramatic given the DAX had gained some 20 percent in the last 10 weeks and a bout of profit-taking had long been anticipated.
Despite 26 of the 30 shares in the DAX index posting losses in the bourse session, telephone monopoly Deutsche Tekelom and carmaker BMW AG bucked the trend.
Telekom ended trade up 1.20 marks at 36.85 marks after hitting a new high at 37 marks. BMW shares hit a new record at 1,312 marks and ended trade up 23.50 marks at 1,291 marks.
London's FTSE 100 index slipped more than half a percentage point to close below the important 4,400 point level at 4,397.7.
"The odds are that the Fed will raise rates at the next meeting," said UK equity strategist Steve Wright. British rates are also likely to head higher during the second half.
"In this interest rate environment, UK equities are probably slightly overvalued," said Wright, who's year end target for the FTSE 100 is 4,300.

A handful of British stocks strongly bucked the weaker market trend, including Enterprise Oil which jumped 16.5 pence to 650, after the company increased the dividend by a bigger margin than most analysts' forecasts and raised its production estimates for 1999.
French shares also probed lower after the U.S. data which one broker called disappointing.
The CAC-40 index closed down 9.60 points, or 0.36 percent, at 2,632.10. The CAC-40 futures contract was down 24.5 at 2,632 from Wednesday's close.
Banking blue chip BNP bounced back, rising 3.7 percent to 272, on short covering after heavy falls earlier this week following rumours that Axa-UAP would lighten its holding.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7059 marks and 123.29 yen, compared with 1.7023 marks and 122.62 yen in late trading on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 24.8 points, or 0.56 percent, at 4,397.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 9.6 points, or 0.36 percent, at 2,632.1.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 65.59 points, or 1.92 percent, at 3,349.81. In later screen trading the IBIS DAX ended 14.58 points lower at 3,367.82.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed up 40 cents at $353.05. Silver finished up three cents at $5.28.
